appearance: A small map-fragment charm — a torn piece of parchment with a single ink line
description: The Cartographer's sigil. Awarded for completing the map of a zone. The line on the fragment connects to the other fragments when placed near them.
rewardEffect: Reveals unexplored areas on the zone map when worn

appearance: A starfield charm — a small dark disc with tiny points of light that only appear in shadow
description: Nyx's sigil. Awarded for understanding that the complete Song is all notes AND all silences. The charm glows only in the dark.
rewardEffect: Creates a small zone of silence around the player — silences ambient noise for contemplation

appearance: A bodhrán charm — a tiny drum that pulses at 50 BPM when held
description: The Pirate's sigil. Awarded for charting the uncharted zones. The Pirate's rhythm, made wearable. The both are: the adequate — the sword and the drum.
rewardEffect: Steadies the player's heartbeat to 50 BPM — the calm tempo. Compass That Points Forward ability.

appearance: A garland charm — a tiny circlet of severed heads, each face different, each face the player's
description: Kali's sigil. Awarded for facing false selves and stopping the destruction. The hardest action: doing nothing.
rewardEffect: Reveals false identities in NPC dialogue — the player can detect when an NPC is performing rather than being

appearance: A music box charm — a tiny mechanism that plays a single note when wound
description: The Guest's sigil. Awarded for helping Death negotiate more time. The note is the one Death MADE, not caught — the note that creates Nyx's silence in the singing vines.
rewardEffect: The player can hear Death's original note — a sound no other character can hear. Reveals hidden passages in the catacombs.

appearance: A crystal charm that holds a faint, ancient light — not the Inn's 42Hz but something older
description: The Constant's sigil. Awarded for understanding that 42Hz is not the first Song — it's the latest. The reward is perspective.
rewardEffect: Reveals the frequency of previous universal cycles — the player can hear echoes of songs that came before 42Hz

appearance: A terrace charm — a tiny carved step that hums at 42Hz when placed on stone
description: The Peruvian Guide's sigil. Awarded for tending the sleeping giant's dream. The terrace is dream-language made visible.
rewardEffect: The player can feel the sleeping giants' dreams — geological vibrations made sensible

appearance: A lighthouse charm — a tiny tower that emits a faint 42Hz pulse at 50 BPM intervals
description: The Owl's sigil. Awarded for the night vigil at the lighthouse. The Beacon ability — guiding other players in deep water.
rewardEffect: Beacon ability — the player's light guides other players in deep water zones. Other players see a faint light when this charm is active.

appearance: A star-glyph charm — a small crystal that holds a single character of the star-language
description: The Zorya's sigil. Awarded for reading the negative space between stars and discovering a NEW word. The Star-Glyph connects to the Shifting Man, the Cartographer, and the Queen of Webs.
rewardEffect: The player can read star-glyphs — the written form of the Song. Unlocks Tier 4 element charm readings on Oceanianoir's skin.

appearance: A mirror charm — a small polished disc that reflects the player's face differently each time
description: The Siren's sigil. Awarded for the Siren hearing her own song for the first time through the Queen of Webs' thread.
rewardEffect: The player can hear their own frequency — a personal tone that is unique to their character. Reveals the Siren's inner voice in coastal zones.

appearance: A hedgehog charm — a tiny rolled creature that uncurls when the player is still for 2 minutes
description: The Greenward's sigil. Awarded for calming Medusa's snakes for one minute so she could see a hedgehog alive. The smallest NPC becomes the largest reward.
rewardEffect: Small creatures in the Inn approach the player when the player is still — the trust extends beyond NPCs to animals

appearance: A bone-brush charm — a tiny brush made from a carved bone handle with ochre-stained bristles
description: The Bone Keeper's sigil. Awarded for learning to see the architecture underneath the living thing.
rewardEffect: The player can see skeletal structures through living things — the bone, the map, and the fossil become visible as overlays

appearance: An amber bead that hums at 42Hz — the Song, made wearable
description: Awarded for completing all main quests in the Cosmology Level. The Song frequency charm. The both are: the adequate — the heard and the worn.
rewardEffect: The player hums at 42Hz — the Song is now carried. NPCs near the player respond to the frequency.

appearance: An obsidian bead — silent, no rattle, no shine, absorbing light
description: Awarded for completing all main quests in the Undercity/In-Between. The Silence frequency charm. The both are: the adequate — the adequate.
rewardEffect: The player can enter silence mode — all ambient sound fades, the SIT mechanic auto-activates

appearance: A carnelian bead — warm, orange-red, pulsing with heat
description: Awarded for completing all main quests in the Norse Zone. The Fire frequency charm. Erik's fire, made wearable.
rewardEffect: The player radiates warmth — cold zones become tolerable, ice melts in the player's presence

appearance: An aquamarine bead — clear blue-green, shimmering like water
description: Awarded for completing all main quests in the Coast/Water System. The Water frequency charm. Persephone's tide, made wearable.
rewardEffect: The player can breathe underwater longer — the tide favors the player. Persephone's bifocal gaze becomes accessible.

appearance: A limestone bead — pale, rough, heavy for its size
description: Awarded for completing all main quests in the Cave City. The Stone frequency charm. The both are: the adequate — the adequate.
rewardEffect: The player can sense geological structures — caves, passages, and hidden chambers become perceptible through vibration

appearance: A moss agate bead — green, organic, with inclusions that look like tiny trees
description: Awarded for completing all main quests in the Canopy City/Garden. The Root frequency charm. The both are: the adequate — the adequate.
rewardEffect: The player can hear the mycorrhizal network — the forest's communication becomes audible. Trade routes become visible.

appearance: A tuning fork charm — a tiny fork that vibrates at 42Hz when struck
description: The Song thread charm. Awarded for completing the main Song storyline. The 42Hz frequency, made wearable.
rewardEffect: The player can hear the Song in every zone — the 42Hz vibration becomes perceptible everywhere

appearance: A hollow bead — a bead that is silent, no rattle, no shine, empty
description: The Silence thread charm. Awarded for completing the Silence storyline. The silence that makes the Song possible.
rewardEffect: The player can enter total silence — the void that precedes the Song. Nyx's silence, worn.

appearance: A ruler-mark charm — a small engraved bar with fine graduations
description: The Measurement thread charm. Awarded for completing the Measurement storyline. The Crone's word: 'Adequate.'
rewardEffect: The player can measure anything — frequencies, distances, times, temperatures. The measurement is the adequate.

appearance: A flame charm — a tiny flame shape that flickers with warm light
description: The Fire thread charm. Awarded for completing the Fire storyline. Erik's fire that welcomes, not consumes.
rewardEffect: The player carries Erik's fire — warmth that welcomes, light that does not consume. The campfire is always available.

appearance: A wave charm — a small wave-drop that shimmers with tidal motion
description: The Water thread charm. Awarded for completing the Water storyline. Persephone's tide, made wearable.
rewardEffect: The player can control tidal cycles — bringing high tide or low tide to water zones at will. The Tide Queen's permission.

appearance: A blank tag — an unengraved tag that the player names themselves
description: The Naming thread charm. Awarded for completing the Naming storyline. The player names the charm — Bastion's act. The naming is the saving.
rewardEffect: The player can name things — naming an NPC, a zone, a creature, or an object gives it a new property. The name IS the magic.

appearance: A root cross-section charm — a small root-slice bead showing the growth rings
description: The Root thread charm. Awarded for completing the Root storyline. The mycorrhizal network, made wearable.
rewardEffect: The player can access the mycorrhizal network from anywhere — the forest's communication is always available.

appearance: A geode slice — a thin geode cross-section showing the crystal interior
description: The Stone thread charm. Awarded for completing the Stone storyline. The geode — the Inn's namesake, made wearable.
rewardEffect: The player can see the crystal interior of any stone — the geode's secret is always visible. Stone identification is automatic.

appearance: A knotted cord charm — a tiny knotted thread that connects to other threads
description: The Thread thread charm. Awarded for completing the Thread storyline. The Queen of Webs' thread, made wearable.
npcConnection: The Queen of Webs / The Siren
rewardEffect: The player can see connections between NPCs, zones, and storylines — the thread that connects everything becomes visible.

appearance: A compass charm — a tiny compass that doesn't point north
description: The Wandering thread charm. Awarded for completing the Wandering storyline. The Compass That Points Forward — the Pirate's reward.
npcConnection: The Pirate / The Wayfarer / The Wayfarer
rewardEffect: The compass points the player toward the next unexplored zone or undiscovered charm. The forward direction is always known.

appearance: A cornerstone charm — a small carved block with the seven base materials etched on its faces
description: The Building thread charm. Awarded for completing the Building storyline. The seven materials — Wood, Stone, Clay, Sand, Ore, Hemp, Thatching.
rewardEffect: The player can build in any zone — all zone-specific building styles are unlocked. The cornerstone is the foundation of everything.

appearance: An artist's palette charm — a tiny palette with nine colors of paint
description: The Embedded thread charm. Awarded for completing the Embedded Artist storyline. The nine artists' styles, made wearable.
rewardEffect: The player can see the embedded artist's influence in any zone — the aesthetic framework becomes visible as an overlay.

appearance: THE EGG — a Fabergé puzzle egg that opens when the player reaches the endgame. The bracelet transforms around it.
description: The Egg thread charm. The final charm. Not given — REVEALED. When the player opens the Egg, the bracelet transforms: the Egg charm appears at the center, and all other charms rearrange around it. The understanding is: the player IS the Inn.
rewardEffect: The bracelet is complete. The complete is the player. The player IS the Inn. All charm effects are permanently active. The Egg opens a final area accessible only to the player who has completed everything.

appearance: A stained-glass fragment — a small piece of colored glass that catches light
description: Tiffany's artist charm. Awarded for completing the Tiffany jigsaw puzzle. The stained-glass fragment connects to the Canopy City's light.
rewardEffect: The charm refracts light in the Inn — colored shadows appear in the player's vicinity

appearance: A swirl bead — a bead with painted swirls that seem to move
description: Van Gogh's artist charm. Awarded for completing the Van Gogh jigsaw puzzle. The swirl connects to the night sky.
rewardEffect: The charm creates a starry-night overlay in dark zones — the swirl is always visible overhead

appearance: A gold-leaf disc — a small disc covered in gold leaf with geometric patterns
description: Klimt's artist charm. Awarded for completing the Klimt jigsaw puzzle. The gold leaf connects to the catacombs' visual language.
rewardEffect: The charm reveals gold-leaf patterns on stone surfaces — the Klimt layer becomes visible

appearance: A tiny silhouette — a dark silhouette figure that changes shape in firelight
description: Bosch's artist charm. Awarded for completing the Bosch jigsaw puzzle. The silhouette connects to Eileen's cave shadows.
rewardEffect: The charm activates Bosch cave shadows on nearby walls — the silhouette shifts with the player's frequency

appearance: A pipe charm — a tiny curved pipe. 'This is not a pipe.'
description: Magritte's artist charm. Awarded for completing the Magritte jigsaw puzzle. The pipe that is not a pipe — the sign that is not the thing.
rewardEffect: The charm reveals the difference between signs and things — NPC names float above them as labels that can be questioned

appearance: A water-lily bead — a soft-edged bead with water-color gradients
description: Monet's artist charm. Awarded for completing the Monet jigsaw puzzle. The water-lily connects to the water zones' light.
rewardEffect: The charm softens all edges in the player's view — the world becomes impressionist, details blur into light

appearance: A cutout shape — a bold paper-cutout shape in vivid color
description: Matisse's artist charm. Awarded for completing the Matisse jigsaw puzzle. The cutout connects to the garden's vivid color.
rewardEffect: The charm increases color saturation — the world becomes more vivid, more Matisse

appearance: A melting clock — a small clock that droops and changes shape
description: Dalí's artist charm. Awarded for completing the Dalí jigsaw puzzle. The melting clock connects to the Inn's time mechanic.
rewardEffect: The charm distorts time perception — the player can slow or speed their experience of time in non-combat zones

appearance: A line-art charm — a black-line filigree piece with intricate curves
description: Beardsley's artist charm. Awarded for completing the Beardsley jigsaw puzzle. The line-art connects to the Art Nouveau aesthetic.
rewardEffect: The charm reveals Art Nouveau patterns on architectural surfaces — the Beardsley layer becomes visible

appearance: A wire-wrapped bead — a stone wrapped in thin copper wire
description: Awarded for learning wire-wrapping from the Artisan Thief. The first crafting technique — the wire that holds the stone.
rewardEffect: The player can upgrade stone charms from Level 1 (raw) to Level 2 (wire-wrapped)

appearance: A set-stone charm — a stone in a metal bezel, a proper jewelry setting
description: Awarded for learning stone-setting from The Mason. The second crafting technique — the metal that holds the stone.
rewardEffect: The player can upgrade stone charms from Level 2 (wire-wrapped) to Level 3 (set stone)

appearance: A forged metal charm — a piece of decorative metalwork
description: Awarded for learning metal-smithing from The Smelter. The third crafting technique — the fire that shapes the metal.
rewardEffect: The player can upgrade stone charms from Level 3 (set stone) to Level 4 (forged setting)

appearance: A woven bead charm — beads woven together in a pattern
description: Awarded for learning beadwork from The Brownies. The fourth crafting technique — the pattern that connects the beads.
rewardEffect: The player can combine multiple stone charms into a single woven piece — the bracelet gains a beadwork section

appearance: An engraved tag — a small metal tag with fine engraving
description: Awarded for learning engraving from Gesso. The fifth crafting technique — the word that marks the work.
rewardEffect: The player can upgrade stone charms from Level 4 (forged) to Level 5 (engraved masterwork). The engraving records the stone's name, the game where it was earned, and the date.
